question: Can a class-balanced, CV-tuned LightGBM model match or beat a standard MLP perception stand-in on macro-F1 while giving lower per-sample inference latency and better accuracy under input noise?
method: Stratified 75/25 split of scikit-learn digits; features standardised on training data. Baseline MLPClassifier (128 hidden units) vs class-balanced LightGBM with n_estimators and learning_rate chosen by 3-fold CV on training data. Test metrics, latency and noisy accuracy computed for both; repeated for seeds 42, 43, 44.
baseline: scikit-learn MLPClassifier, one hidden layer of 128 units, trained on standardised pixels
improved: Class-balanced LightGBM classifier; n_estimators and learning_rate selected by 3-fold stratified CV on the training split only
notes: Digits is a small stand-in for camera perception, not a driving dataset, so results do not show real-world performance. Noise is Gaussian sigma=2.0 on the raw pixel scale, one fixed draw shared by both models. Latency is mean wall-clock time per single-sample predict() over 200 test rows on this runner (LightGBM single-threaded); it is hardware-dependent. Std values are across seeds [42, 43, 44]; the test split is identical for all. Chosen LightGBM params per seed: [{'learning_rate': 0.1, 'n_estimators': 100}, {'learning_rate': 0.1, 'n_estimators': 100}, {'learning_rate': 0.1, 'n_estimators': 100}].
